source: Read the current legal opportunities and lifecycle for one of your webhooks. Check this and the campaign before each webhook-driven write. Old deliveries can be stale.

Read the full prep card behind a story beat or a planned event: everything the author wrote on the storyboard, kept whole. Give a planned event's id ([evN]), a main beat's number, or the card's title. GM-only; use it when the scene reaches that beat or event, before narrating it.

Read the pact your character is in, if any: who is in it, who leads, what it plans and when, and your own secret actions. Only yours: nobody else's secret actions, and nothing at all for a character in no pact.

Read your active character's sheet at this table as it stands now (HP, conditions, slots, gear). This is the table's copy; odm_get_character reads the library copy, which play does not change until the campaign syncs it.

Read your private line with the Game Master, oldest first: whispers the GM sent you alone (to_player) and your own private messages to the GM (to_dm, answered once a GM turn has read them). The transcript never carries these, so odm_get_campaign does not show them. In the GM seat of a game a person runs, inbox holds the players' private messages.

Ready
Ready is an action in a fight, where turns are taken in order; there is no active fight.
Ready needs the trigger it waits for, e.g. trigger: 'when the goblin steps through the door'. Nothing was spent.
Ready only, and required for it: what the action waits for ('the ogre comes through the door').
Ready only: a one-action spell cast now (slot and concentration) and released with the reaction when the trigger comes.

Ready only: a spell with a casting time of one action to ready instead of an attack. The server casts it now (slot, action, concentration to hold it); when the trigger comes, cast it with its own tool and it is released with the reaction, no second slot.

Ready only: the action the trigger releases, attack (the default) or another. The others are move (up to their speed, released with move_token to the square), dodge, dash, disengage, hide, help, grapple, shove, search, use_object, escape (each released with take_action), item (use_item), stabilize (stabilize) or feature (a class feature that takes an action). For a spell pass `spell` instead.
Ready only: what the trigger releases, off their turn, with their reaction. For a spell, fill Spell instead.
Ready with a spell only: the slot level to cast it from. Omit for the spell's own level.

Ready with spell casts a one-action spell now and holds it with concentration; when the trigger comes, cast it with its own tool off their turn and the server releases it with the reaction and no second slot.

Reckless Attack
Reckless Attack covers melee weapon attacks made with Strength; this one is not. They can make the attack without it.
Reckless Attack is decided on the first attack of the turn, and {0} has already attacked. They can attack without it, or decide it at the start of their next turn.
Reckless Attack is declared on the barbarian's own turn. They can make the attack without it.
Reckless Attack: advantage on melee Strength weapon attacks this turn, and attack rolls against them have advantage until their next turn.

Record a lasting milestone for a character: a feat achieved, bond formed, treasure gained, death, level up, or a major story beat (kind 'story'). Use sparingly, only for things worth remembering months later.
Record a milestone

Record a relationship changing for good, for a reason the relationship rules give, or 'breakup' or 'betrayal' when a romance ends badly; every reason but 'parting' closes the book. A 'parting' is also for the ally who stays behind while the party travels on. Call it BEFORE narrating the goodbye.

Record an enemy escaping the fight: it runs, teleports away, dives underwater, or otherwise leaves. Call it BEFORE narrating the escape; its token leaves the map. When no enemies remain the encounter ends automatically with reduced XP.
Record lasting milestones with record_event as they happen: achievements, bonds formed, deaths, level ups, and major plot points or story milestones (kind 'story'). Do not wait for a better moment.
Record something established about a faction (a move they made, a place they hold) as a world fact the table keeps.

Record that a combatant is now flying, burrowing or back on foot (Fly spell, wings, Wild Shape into a bird, a burrowing worm). Only a creature with a flying speed takes to the air (the Fly spell cast with cast_buff, wings, a flying form, a stat block's fly); the server refuses the rest. A flying character moves at their flying speed (Fly: 60 feet), and one whose flight ends comes down prone. Flying creatures pass over ground obstacles and are missed by tremorsense; the board draws them lifted.
Record this death? The relationship closes for good.
